question: When combining multiple node overrides in a single agent, what pattern should every override follow?
options: Buffer all data until the pipeline completes, then process it
Call Agent.default to run the standard behavior, then add custom logic around it
Skip the default and delegate to the next node directly
Replace the default implementation entirely with custom logic
explanation: Every node override follows the same pattern: call Agent.default to invoke the built-in implementation, add custom logic around it (before, after, or filtering), and yield the results. This keeps each concern isolated and lets you disable any override without affecting the others.

question: When testing pipeline node overrides, what should you test — the provider behavior or your custom logic?
options: Your custom override logic, by mocking the default implementation and verifying your transformations
The provider behavior to ensure Deepgram and GPT-4o work correctly
Both equally, with real API calls in every test
explanation: You are not testing whether Deepgram transcribes correctly or GPT-4o reasons well. You are testing that your overrides correctly intercept, transform, and pass through data. Mock the provider responses (via Agent.default) and verify that your filtering, enrichment, and transformation logic works correctly.
